title: VIP Intake Adjudicator and Sprint-Fit Calculator
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and deliver a structured intake and adjudication flow for VIP/top-account change requests that combines a quantitative score with a sprint-fit calculator. The output should be a deterministic routing decision: Fast-track, Deferred + Commitment Window, or Not Accepted. This ticket covers the scoring model, required data inputs, UI hints for the intake form, adjudication SLA windows, and a light-weight implementation plan for Cycle 2025-W12.
background: We receive a steady stream of high-touch requests from strategic accounts asking for prioritization on the roadmap. Current handling is ad-hoc: PMs triage via email and Slack, engineering feedback is slow, and customers are left without predictable commitments. Existing priority playbooks are descriptive but lack a reproducible numeric adjudication and a simple engineering-fit calculator to decide if a piece fits into the next N sprints. This creates scope creep and negotiation overhead.
goals: Create a repeatable, transparent decision algorithm that surface trade-offs to customers and internal stakeholders
Reduce PM adjudication time for VIP requests to under 72 hours on average
Provide an automated sprint-fit estimate to indicate likely delivery lanes (next sprint / next quarter / backlog)
Increase on-time delivery predictability for accepted VIP items by 30% over baseline
success_metrics: % of VIP requests receiving definitive routing within SLA >= 90%
Forecast accuracy (planned vs actual delivery window) improvement >= 30%
Reduction in email/Slack follow-ups per VIP ticket by 40%
intake_workflow: Step 1: Customer-facing intake form (Console: VIP Intake) with structured fields: business outcome, impacted user segments, ARR/expansion uplift estimate, urgency reason, security/compliance constraints, required uptime, proposed go-live window
Step 2: Auto-enrich intake via account signals (ARR, contract expiry, recent escalations, usage delta) from CRM and telemetry
Step 3: Compute preliminary score and sprint-fit; surface in PM queue with recommended routing
Step 4: Adjudication call only for items in 'Borderline' band (score near threshold) — no-call auto-accept for clear 'Fast-track' and auto-defer for clear 'Backlog' buckets
Step 5: Publish outcome to customer (with rationale and commitment runway if accepted) and create Engineering acceptance task if approved
scoring_algorithm: Score components (normalized 0-100) and final score = 0.4*Commercial + 0.25*Strategic + 0.2*CustomerRisk + 0.15*ImplementationFit. Commercial = min(100, ARR*10k scaling); Strategic = binary*100 for partner/market-impact plus product-strategy alignment multiplier (0-1). CustomerRisk = inverse of customer workarounds (higher risk -> higher score). ImplementationFit = estimated story points normalized inversely (lower points -> higher fit). Thresholds: >=75 -> Fast-track; 55-74 -> Borderline (adjudicate); <55 -> Backlog. Documented examples attached to model for calibration. Use rolling calibration weekly for first 6 weeks against actual outcomes.
sprint_fit_calculator: Inputs: estimated story points, cross-team dependencies (count), infra work (bool), security review need (bool), regression risk (low/med/high). Heuristic: EffectivePoints = story_points + (dependencies*3) + (infra?5:0) + (security_review?4:0) + (regression_risk == 'high'?3: regression_risk == 'med'?1:0). Sprint fit mapping: EffectivePoints <= 8 => likely next sprint; 9-20 => next 2-3 sprints; >20 => next quarter/backlog. Provide confidence bands (+/- one sprint) and flag blockers automatically.
acceptance_criteria: A customer-facing VIP Intake form exists in Console with required structured fields and inline help text
Automated enrichment pipeline attaches ARR and usage signals to intake submissions
Scoring engine computes a reproducible score and recommended routing per document algorithm
Sprint-fit calculator returns a deterministic lane and confidence band
Adjudication SLA: automatic routing for clear buckets; PM adjudication responses created for 'Borderline' items within 72 hours
Outcome notifications automatically sent to submitting contact with rationale and next steps
Dashboard: weekly VIP intake metrics and calibration table visible to PM/Eng leadership
tasks: PM: Finalize intake form fields + inline help (Confluence draft)
Data Eng: Build enrichment job to attach ARR, usage delta, contract dates to submissions (weekly sync)
Eng: Implement scoring and sprint-fit microservice (read-only mode behind feature flag)
Design: Console UI for VIP Intake and outcome modal + email templates
SRE: Define alerting for auto-accept false positives and SLA misses
PM/Eng: Calibration plan (6-week cadence) and retrospective after initial run
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1-2): Internal beta — PMs and Solutions Eng only. Collect 20 sample intakes and calibrate weights
Phase 2 (Week 3-4): Invite top 15 strategic accounts (opt-in). Monitor adjudication SLAs and adjust heuristics
Phase 3 (Week 5+): Open to all top-account lanes. Soft launch notification + playbook for CSMs
Phase 4: Q2 retrospective; fold into standard roadmap intake and handoff to Committed Roadmap process
monitoring_and_kpis: Adjudication latency (time from submission to outcome)
Distribution of scores and % in each bucket
Delivery window accuracy (predicted vs actual sprint) per cohort
Customer satisfaction for VIP intake (CSAT post-outcome)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model biases overweight ARR and ignore strategic product fit -> Mitigation: include qualitative Strategic multiplier and weekly calibration
Risk: Engineering rejects auto-accepted items due to hidden infra work -> Mitigation: flag security/infra booleans on intake and require Eng quick-verify within 48 hours
Risk: Customers perceive numeric score as opaque -> Mitigation: include rationale paragraph and example trade-offs in every outcome email
Risk: Gaming submissions to inflate ARR numbers -> Mitigation: auto-verify ARR from CRM and mark mismatches for review
open_questions: What exact ARR scaling factor maps to Commercial component? (proposal: 10k->1 point up to cap)
Should Solutions Eng have veto power on auto-accepts? (ops/scale implications)
What's the SLA for engineering verification on auto-accepted items that require infra/SEC review?
Do we surface raw score to customers or only the routing decision and rationale?
